I've thought about that before too, but music, like literature, and really any form of art is virtually limitless. Given the different instruments, genres, styles, etc. I'm pretty sure it would be mathematically "impossible" to produce two songs that sounded 90% + alike out of pure coincidence.

As for "good" and "bad" taste regarding music, it ebbs and flows. Some people feel that 60s/70s Rock was the height of musical achievement. For others, it's the classical era of Europe. And for others it's 90s Soul, 80s Pop, etc, etc, the list goes on and on into eternity. Some years and even decades have been considered "bad" for music and others "good". Obviously all of that is a matter of opinion, but I think the general population of people can come to a consensus on what time periods produced more good music than another time period. And a lot of those opinions come down to the general culture and happenings of the time.

Is it a period of war or peace? Is the economy good or bad? Is the government free and transparent, or restrictive and tyrannical? Are people more or less religious? What movies are popular? Myriads of factors play a a role in the music, and art in general that is produced. So long as the aforementioned factors are changing, art will continue to as well.

To sum all of my rambling up. No. Music will never go stale and artists will always be coming up with new and creative (or cliche and dull) tunes for humanity to jam out to for as long as we exist!
